topics.topic: How outcome_unknown is represented in EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS and resolved using contextual state
questions: What single table value does the `outcome_unknown` status map to, and which module combines it with the EffectAttempt state and binding output shape to obtain the actual element conclusion?
How can a total table keyed only by NodeExecution status represent the context-dependent conclusion of `outcome_unknown`?
What table entry applies to `outcome_unknown`, whose conclusion is waiting, succeeded, or failed depending on the associated EffectAttempt resolution and whether the binding has output ports?

quotes:
`EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS` (row `StatusConclusion`, key `status`,
      total): every NodeExecutionStatus with its NodeConclusion. The seven
      failures of A13 rule 5 conclude `failed`; `service_unreachable` and
      `outcome_unknown` are waits (A13 rule 5), an unresolved one concluding
      `waiting` and a resolved one as A11 rule 3 says; `refused_by_owner`
      concludes `refused`, which makes the run `refused` (A10); a
      `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed` record concludes so. An
      operation element is still judged by `operation_element_conclusion`
      alone (A13 rule 7); the table is the reading of a status, not a second
      judgment of the operation.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id — after an attempt resolved not_applied only one whose attempt_number is greater than that of the element's latest attempt so resolved, the same attempt rule find_send_authority applies to approvals; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; otherwise — no NodeExecution, or a latest outcome_unknown whose attempt the owner resolved not_applied — the element is not reached, so it is reached again when its node is next taken, and after not_applied its send needs a fresh approval (find_send_authority), which reach_operation_element requests (decision 32).
judgement.why: State 6 makes the table only the basic status reading and leaves the contextual operation conclusion to `effects.operation_element_conclusion`.

topics.topic: Whether HTTP_METHOD_BODIES cells are booleans or members of a named body-policy type
questions: Are the cells of `HTTP_METHOD_BODIES` booleans, or members of a new closed body-policy enumeration?
What model member type do the cells of `HTTP_METHOD_BODIES` name?
What model member represents whether a method carries a body, since the decision is Boolean but no body-policy enumeration or row model is named?

quotes:
`HTTP_METHOD_BODIES` (row `HttpMethodBody`, key `method`, total): every
      HttpMethod and whether its request carries the inputs not used in the
      path as a body (A09 rule 2); without one they become query parameters.

check_request_shape: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Judges the ports by their declarations alone, in this order, and answers with fits false and a reason naming the first failing rule: first every placeholder segment of the path, the placeholders taken in name order by Unicode code point, must name an input port whose value_schema declares type string or integer; then, only for an http_method whose row of the imported HTTP_METHOD_BODIES constant has carries_body false, input ports in name order by Unicode code point must have no file carriage and every input that is not a placeholder must have a value_schema whose type is string, integer, number, boolean or null, or array whose items declare one of those types; then an output port of file carriage must be the only output port and must have cardinality one.
judgement.why: The later contract names the `HttpMethodBody` row and its Boolean `carries_body` field.

topics.topic: The exact schema, taxonomy, and values of NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
questions: What exact model enumerations and total row shape does `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS` use, including success, guard skip, failure, refusal and each wait state?
What are the table's exact key, columns, and cell values, including the distinct effects of success, `skipped_by_guard`, failure, and waiting on run completion and dependant readiness?

quotes:
`NodeConclusion` (`60_model_closure_domain.json`): `succeeded`,
      `failed`, `waiting`, `refused`, `skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed` —
      what an element or a node has concluded (A13 rules 5 and 7). Not
      reached is no conclusion and is not a member. `ElementConclusion` stays
      the union `effects` answers; its discriminator is the variant, not this
      taxonomy.

`NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS` (row `ConclusionEffect`, key `conclusion`,
      total): `lets_run_succeed` — a run that ends without waits succeeds
      when every node's conclusion has it (A13 rule 7: `succeeded`,
      `skipped_by_guard`); `fails_dependants` — a node with an input from a
      node whose conclusion has it concludes `upstream_failed` (A13 rule 5:
      `failed`, `upstream_failed`). One table, because both readings are
      asked of every new conclusion together; `waiting` and `refused` have
      neither, since a waiting node's dependants wait and a refused run
      derives nothing.
judgement.why: State 6 defines the key enumeration, row type, columns, and the values for every conclusion.

topics.topic: Which module owns the conclusion/effect correspondence policy versus merely supplying or applying it
questions: Which module owns the A13 correspondences, and is `data_provider` a newly added A13 owner/consumer or merely a provider of values whose meaning remains owned by `run_graph`?
Which module owns the policy that maps execution statuses to conclusions and conclusions to their effects, and which module merely applies or exposes it?

quotes:
The table
is the one mapping;

What code reads about the
members of such an enumeration — the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives
(A13 rules 5 and 7), what each node conclusion means for the run and for its
dependants (A13 rules 5 and 7), the status a run rests in for each wait reason
(A13 rule 8), whether an HTTP method carries a body (A09 rule 2) — is a
correspondence over that taxonomy (SPEC_STANDARD 15.2): a table here keyed by
the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members.
judgement.why: The declared one ownership mapping omits `data_provider` from A13 while the module section assigns it ownership of A13 correspondence tables.

topics.topic: Which row models and closed enumerations type the conclusion correspondence tables and whether models owns them
questions: What row models and enumerations type `EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS` and `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS`, and does `models` own these additional types?
What are the exact row models and closed enumerations for node conclusions and their run/dependant effects, since M01–M28 define no NodeConclusion or NodeConclusionEffect model or enumeration?

quotes:
`NodeConclusion` (`60_model_closure_domain.json`): `succeeded`,
      `failed`, `waiting`, `refused`, `skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed` —
      what an element or a node has concluded (A13 rules 5 and 7). Not
      reached is no conclusion and is not a member. `ElementConclusion` stays
      the union `effects` answers; its discriminator is the variant, not this
      taxonomy.

`EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS` (row `StatusConclusion`, key `status`,
      total): every NodeExecutionStatus with its NodeConclusion.

`NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS` (row `ConclusionEffect`, key `conclusion`,
      total): `lets_run_succeed` — a run that ends without waits succeeds
      when every node's conclusion has it (A13 rule 7: `succeeded`,
      `skipped_by_guard`); `fails_dependants` — a node with an input from a
      node whose conclusion has it concludes `upstream_failed` (A13 rule 5:
      `failed`, `upstream_failed`).

State 1 (2026-10-18, decision 33): the enumeration `NodeConclusion` and the
  row models `StatusConclusion`, `ConclusionEffect`, `WaitReasonRestingStatus`
  and `HttpMethodBody`. Reopens the rounds of State 1.
judgement.why: State 6 names the additional model-owned enumeration and row models that type both tables.
